Project Goal

Tapeology is a **standalone, real-time tape-reading system for US stocks**. It does one thing well: given a single ticker, it watches live order flow — trades, quotes, and (later) the Level 2 book — and classifies the **current tape state**.

Session i_will_be_super_rich

5 iterations · 18/20 journeys passing · 41 min wall time
Goal achieved. Read the “What we delivered” wrap →

The story so far

Project story so far

Tapeology is a real-time tape-reading tool for US stocks: you point it at one ticker and it tells you, in plain language, what the order flow is doing right now — and how sure it is.

How it has grown

An earlier run built the practice mode first, proving the hard ideas on a deterministic simulator before touching real market data. The single-ticker cockpit came to life — a live quote, a running trade list, the core flow readouts, a confidence score, plain-language observations, and an event log. The product's defining habit of honesty was established early: it recognizes when heavy buying or selling is being absorbed (the price refuses to move) rather than mistaking that pressure for control.

This session then set out to bring in real US market data through that same engine without ever inventing a number. Real data arrived in stages. First came a data-source selector (Live, Historical, or Simulated), each revealing only the controls it needs. Then real historical replays: enter a US stock, pick a past date and window, and watch that session's real trades and quotes flow through the unchanged engine — including honest error messages for every dead end (unknown symbol, empty window, closed market). After wiring symbol search and market-clock awareness, the session completed the live promise: the cockpit can stream a real ticker live, showing a green "live" light during market hours and an amber "stale" light during any quiet gap — inventing no trades during the lull, and recovering cleanly when real data resumes. Those sixteen journeys reached a milestone at iteration 4.

Iteration 5 tackled the directional accuracy of real-data prints: roughly one in five real-market trades had been showing "unknown" — those landing between the bid and ask, or arriving before any quote was in effect. A two-stage aggressor classifier now closes that gap, applying the published quote first and falling back to the tick test when that cannot decide. On the committed real Ford data window, unknown prints dropped from 20% to zero.

Iteration 6 added the prediction chart: a candlestick price chart now appears above the cockpit whenever you watch a simulated or replayed stock. The engine accumulates every watched trade price into candle bars at 10, 30, or 60 seconds each, and drops a colored marker at the exact moment the tape state shifts to something meaningful — green for buyer control, rose for seller control, amber for absorption. A bar-size selector lets you switch granularity on the fly. The backend data pipeline was fully proven correct, but a corrupted dev-server cache prevented the browser from actually rendering the chart canvas during QA.

Iteration 7 resolved both outstanding gaps at once. The prediction chart render was confirmed with real browser screenshots — the "is the canvas ever drawn?" question answered with actual pixels, showing emerald rising candles and a buyer-control marker on a live frontend. At the same time, Pause/Resume shipped: a new amber Pause button beside Stop freezes the cockpit, chart, trade list, and tape state at a chosen moment without closing the session, and Resume picks up exactly where things left off — no invented data fills the gap. An honest amber "paused" indicator replaces the green "live" dot while frozen. Nineteen new backend tests and verified browser screenshots back both advances. Eighteen of the twenty must-have journeys now pass.

What it can do today

The product lets users watch one US stock at a time — in practice (simulated) mode, a real past session replayed at a chosen speed, or a real live feed — and read the tape in plain language: buyer control, seller control, bid or ask absorption, or an unclear tape, each with a confidence score, live quote, running trades list, and observations. Users can search for a stock by name, choose the data source, replay history at any speed, and follow a live market with an honest live/stale signal. Most real-market prints carry a buy or sell label. For simulated and historical watches, a candlestick price chart appears above the cockpit with colored tape-state markers and a 10/30/60-second bar-size selector. Users can pause a running watch to study the chart at a specific moment, then resume without losing state or seeing invented data.
